lines.text: Hi, I'm Sindy! Let's run an MPI program across several nodes.
MPI codes need more than one node to test, and you'd rather not wait for the production cluster. sind gives you three workers in Docker.
The default node image ships a full MPI stack, with Open MPI, PMIx and UCX, and Slurm launches with PMIx.
First, a cluster with three workers. Run sind create cluster with this configuration.
Here's the program, a hello world in C.
Every rank looks up its own number, and how many ranks there are in total.
After a barrier, where all ranks wait for each other, every rank prints one line with its host name.
Build it with mpicc, the compiler wrapper that adds the MPI flags for you.
Then srun launches one task per worker node.
Three ranks, one per worker! The order of the lines may vary.
Notice: srun got no MPI option. PMIx is already the default in the slurm.conf that sind generates.
The same program also runs as a batch job. This script asks for three nodes, one task per node, and calls srun.
You hand it to sbatch with the wait flag, which returns once the job has ended. Then cat prints its output file.
So, the MPI stack is built in, srun needs no extra flags, and batch jobs work the same way.
Next up, the MCP integration guide. See you there!
